messages:
Marta Ruiz: Quick triage thread 1: Nebula-7B conversion (Mistral->Qwen layout) showing systematic hallucination after ~48 tokens on some summarization prompts.
Ben Cho: Any repro commands and a failing example?
Marta Ruiz: conversion snippet and small diff below.
```
python convert.py --src mistral-nebula7b.pth --dst qwen/nebula7b.onnx --permute-heads interleave --quant int4
```
Gold fp16: "The committee concluded that the policy would be delayed until June."
Quantized Qwen int4: "The committee concluded that the policy would be delayed until Ju1."
(Inserted combining dot above? weird ligature / unicode composition around token index 50)
Dee Patel: Combining dot above sounds like Unicode normalization/byte-level tokenizer export mismatch. Which tokenizer version/export script did you use?
Marta Ruiz: We used tokenizers v0.12 and a legacy export shim. Not NFKC canonicalized. Also saw a correlated spike in cosine similarity drop of attention weights at layer 10 heads 2-5.
Omar Farouk: Head interleave permute + per-head quant scales can change relative magnitude across interleaved groups, which can shift rotary phase mapping. If the rotary implementation assumes contiguous head ordering but weight permute is interleaving, angles end up applied to wrong subvectors.
Ben Cho: Two quick experiments: 1) run conversion with `--no-permute` to see if interleave is culprit, 2) run with `--preserve-tokenizer` (embed original tokenizer binary into model bundle) to rule out ligature.
Marta Ruiz: Results: `--no-permute` -> soft fail (much closer to gold, no ligature), `--preserve-tokenizer` -> ligature fixed but hallucination still present on long prompts. So we have two orthogonal issues.
Dee Patel: For the hallucination trace, can you dump KV-cache similarity metrics? If the KV keys are scrambled due to head reorder, later attention queries may attend to wrong cached keys, causing drift.
Marta Ruiz: KV similarity plot attached (pasted numbers): layer10 head3 cosine between FP16 vs int4 cached K at time 60 = 0.62 (expected ~0.98).
Omar Farouk: That's a smoking gun. Proposal: converter should also remap rotary angle buffers and KV scale metadata when doing head permutes. Also ensure quant calibration collects per-head statistics before applying permutation.
Ben Cho: Agreed. Additional mitigation: add an adapter in the runtime that detects head-order mismatch via a small checksum test run at load and optionally auto-remap scales/angles if mismatch detected. Saves immediate hotfix in converter.
Dee Patel: Also add tokenizer export step to CI: canonicalize to NFKC and run a tiny roundtrip test: tokenize->detokenize should be identity for a set of punctuation-heavy examples. Failing samples should block conversion.
Marta Ruiz: I'll prototype: 1) converter flag `--remap-for-interleave` that remaps rotary and KV scale tables; 2) loader check that validates head-order checksum and logs a warning; 3) add NFKC canonicalizer to tokenizer-export.
ci-bot: test/nebula-conversion-smoke started.
Marta Ruiz: Perf note: remap adds ~0.15ms/token at conversion time but zero runtime overhead. Calibration requires shooting ~200 random tokens; costly but needed to compute per-head scales.
Ben Cho: When you open the PR, include a before/after eval on summarization (ROUGE L, BLEU) and on the hallucination prompt set. Also include kv-cache cosine matrices.
Marta Ruiz: Will do. Owner: @Marta implement, @Omar review remap logic, @Dee add tokenizer CI and tests, @Ben collect eval numbers. Target: landing into staging quant build in two business days. :shipit:
